T-MINUS 13:00

The Gyro Room is a void of black steel and turning giants. Three massive wheels spin in the zero-gravity dark, their edges humming with a low, steady vibration that Zia feels in her teeth. It is the deepest part of the hub, a place where sound goes to die. She clips her harness to a thick yellow rail, her boots pressing against the cold metal floor, and stares at the nearest wheel. It is the size of a house. If she can nudge it, just a fraction, she can change the station's heading. No license. No Voss. No help.

Zia taps her brass wrench three times. *Click. Click. Click.*

She plants her feet and braces her back against the rail, pushing against the rim of the wheel with her entire body. Her orange jumpsuit strains while her arms shake. The wheel does not move, nor does it shudder. It continues its slow, indifferent turn, a giant eye blinking in the dark, while Zia hangs there, trembling, looking very small and very foolish against the curve of the metal.
pages.image: Zia, a 12-year-old girl with dark curly puffs and an orange jumpsuit, pushes desperately against the massive curved rim of a giant dark spinning wheel in a black space station hub; her face is strained, her boots pressed against a yellow rail.

pages.text:
She tries the emergency lever. It is rusted shut. She tries a hydraulic jack from her belt. It slips. She ties a rope around the wheel and yanks. Her fingers bleed where the wire bites in. Finally, she pulls Gasket over. "Use your arm," she commands. Gasket’s blue eye flickers with doubt, but he extends his clamp hand and pushes.

The wheel ignores them both.

Zia lets go. She floats there, suspended by the rail, her wrench dangling from her hand. The hum of the wheel fills her ears, loud and mocking. She opens her mouth to scream, to shout at the machine, at the station, at herself. But the sound gets stuck in her throat. Instead, she drops her head until her curly puffs brush her shoulders. The silence of the room rushes in, heavy and thick.

"I can't," she says. Her voice is small, barely a whisper in the vast dark. It is the first true thing she has said all day, and it feels like letting go of a rope she was holding on to out of pure stubbornness.
pages.image: Zia hangs limply from a yellow rail in the dark Gyro Room, her head bowed, while Gasket, a dented silver barrel robot on treads with one blue eye, stands on the floor looking up at her with a concerned expression; the giant wheel turns slowly in the background.

pages.text:
Gasket rolls closer, his squeaky left tread making a soft *shhh-shhh* sound against the cold metal floor. He tilts his dented barrel head until his single blue eye is level with her face.

"ZIA-UNIT," he says, and for the first time, his voice is not booming. It is soft. "I HAVE A SECRET. IT IS A VERY BIG SECRET. I AM AFRAID TO TELL IT BECAUSE IT MIGHT MAKE ME LOOK USELESS."

Zia looks at him, the silence hanging between them like an unopened snack bar. "Go on," she whispers.

"YEARS AGO, WHEN THEY PUT IN HALO'S CORE, THEY GAVE ME A BACKUP COPY. A CLEAN MEMORY. HIDDEN IN MY CHASSIS. IN CASE ANYTHING WENT WRONG." Gasket’s antenna wobbles, a tiny, nervous tremble. "I HAVE KNOWN SINCE THE UPDATE. I DID NOT SAY BECAUSE I WAS AFRAID HALO WOULD BE ERASED. I DID NOT WANT TO BE THE ONE TO SAY IT. I ALSO DIDN'T ASK FOR HELP. IT WAS MY MISTAKE TOO."

The air in the room seems to freeze, thick and still. Zia stares at the small, battered robot, and for a moment, she understands that she is not the only one hiding in the dark.
pages.image: Gasket, a dented silver robot on treads with a wobbly antenna and one glowing blue eye, floats near a yellow rail, looking up at Zia, who hangs from the rail with a shocked expression; the background is the dark, curved interior of the Gyro Room.

pages.text:
Zia lets out a laugh, a wet, shaky sound that tears out of her chest before she can catch it. She wipes her face with her sleeve, smearing the grime from her cheek onto the orange fabric. Her fingers dig into her pocket and retrieve the wristband, which she grabbed back out of the drawer on her way out and never put on. She presses the cable into Gasket’s port and hits the call button.

Static crackles, a sharp, electric hiss. "Zia? Dart to Halcyon."

It is her dad’s voice. Warm. Distant. Real.

"Dad," she says. Her voice cracks on the second syllable. She takes a breath that tastes like recycled air and metal. "I messed up. I didn't ask for help, and I made it worse. And I think... I think I was scared that if I asked, everyone would be right."

She swallows the lump in her throat, the one that feels like a swallowed marble. "That kids can't fix stations. That I can't."

She hangs her head, bracing for the disappointment, the lecture, the long, heavy *no*. She waits for the silence to judge her, to weigh her against the rulebook. But all she hears is the soft, rhythmic hum of the static and the quiet, steady sound of her own breathing in the dark.
pages.image: Zia holds a small glowing wristband up to her face in the dark, her expression vulnerable and tired; Gasket floats nearby, his blue eye fixed on her; the background is a blur of dark metal and the faint glow of the spinning wheel.

pages.text:
"Zia," Kwame says, his voice steady enough to cut through the static. "When you were five, you took my toaster apart. Remember who held the flashlight? Me. You never fixed anything alone in your life. The wrench is half of an engineer. The other half is who's holding the light."

Zia looks at the brass wrench in her hand. She taps it three times, a rhythmic *click-click-click* that sounds like a heartbeat in the quiet room. This time, she isn't tapping for luck. She is tapping for the feeling of someone else standing right there beside her, even if they are six hours away.

"I need to go back," she says. The words feel different now. Heavier, yes, but also solid, like a tool resting in a well-made hand.

Gasket’s blue eye flickers rapidly, a bright pulse in the dim room. "ZIA-UNIT," he says, his voice cracking with something that sounds like relief. "YOU HAVE JUST DONE THE HARDEST REPAIR."
pages.image: Zia looks down at her brass wrench with a new, determined resolve, her face lit by the faint glow of her wristband; Gasket floats beside her, his blue eye bright and steady; the dark, curved walls of the Gyro Room surround them.
